- If sentiment history shows positive sentiment (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows steady, flat 30d forecast with no upward trend, true outcome often spikes later; add 2–5% upward bias in later periods.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overcorrects and underpredicts; add 5–10% upward bias to offset lag.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 85), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- If sentiment history is neutral or negative (0.00), model often underperforms; increase forecast by 3–7% to account for market inertia.
- For 30d forecasts with low volatility in history, true outcome often exceeds model by 5–15% in later days; apply 5–10% upward bias for 3–5 days after forecast.
- If model forecast is below 80 and true outcome rises above 85, model is likely underestimating supply/demand shock; increase forecast by 5–10% for next 3 days.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive 0.00 values, model tends to be overly conservative; add 2–5% upward bias to forecast.
